body.statement:
Yes.  For every fixed finite \((\mathcal W,\mathcal Z)\), there is a one-copy structural compiler \(\mathscr A\) with the following properties.  It first rejects any cell rank exceeding two.  A rank-two cell is represented by its two oriented segment modes, refined by all coefficient support faces.  A rank-one cell is represented by the disjoint \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) modes of \(\mathrm{lem:rank\text{-}one\text{-}lred\text{-}normal\text{-}forms}\), with the \(\mathrm E\) split refined coordinatewise.  Products of the four local modes use one shared variable \(b_i\) at each response vertex and are refined by proxy supports, endpoint equalities and inequalities, observed-line incidences, and all nonzero pivots.  Their union is exactly \(\mathcal C_A(T)\).  In design B, adjoining \(\rho\), the zero-residual or active negatively proportional state at each response type, lexicographic nonzero pivots, forest propagation, the active-cycle product-one constraint, positive component scales, normalization, and a signed relevance witness gives a finite union equal exactly to \(\mathcal C_B(T)\).

On each nonempty one-copy chart, \(\mathscr A\) computes descriptions and sample points for all semialgebraically connected components before forming the graph \(t=\tau_C\) and projecting it.  On a component with sampled target \(t_0\), it decides and, when possible, samples the refinement \(\tau_C\ne t_0\).  Thus it decides target constancy within every component and compares the exact constants across all components and charts.  It returns incompatibility when the relevant union is empty, an exact common target when all values agree, and otherwise two cycle points with different targets and their legal full-SCM lifts.  The computation uses no generic two-copy unequal-target predicate.  Over an arbitrary real input field \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), termination is relative to effective arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles.  A target is reported as a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) only when that expression is actually constructed; otherwise it is reported by a real-univariate representation and Thom sign data over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).
body.proof_tex:
We prove structural exhaustiveness before invoking any real-algebraic component routine.

First compute the rank of each \(T_e\).  A sum of the two rank-one matrices \(b_ia_{ei}^{\top}\) and \(b_ja_{ej}^{\top}\) has rank at most two, so a rank exceeding two makes the cycle fiber empty.  Rank zero is excluded by selected-table positivity.  Thus only ranks one and two can occur on a nonempty fiber.

Fix a rank-two cell \(e\) with \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\).  Its normalized columns
\[
c_{ez}=\frac{T_e(\cdot,z)}{v_e(z)}
\]
lie on the observable affine line \(\mathcal L_e\).  In any factorization, \(b_i\ne b_j\), both endpoints lie on \(\mathcal L_e\), and every \(c_{ez}\) lies in the closed segment \([b_i,b_j]\).  Conversely, these segment conditions determine nonnegative coefficients: if \(h_e\) is any coordinate separating the endpoints, then
\[
a_{ei}(z)=v_e(z)
 \frac{c_{ez}(h_e)-b_j(h_e)}{b_i(h_e)-b_j(h_e)},
\qquad
a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)-a_{ei}(z). \tag{2}
\]
The two possible orders of the endpoints are precisely the two orientations used in \(\mathrm{thm:rank\text{-}two\text{-}orientation\text{-}atlas}\).  Replacing each weak coefficient inequality in (2) by the alternatives zero or strictly positive enumerates every forced-zero face.

For a rank-one cell, \(\mathrm{lem:rank\text{-}one\text{-}lred\text{-}normal\text{-}forms}\) proves that the four displayed modes are disjoint and exhaustive.  Notice in particular that mode \(\mathrm L\) leaves the inactive endpoint \(b_i\) unrestricted except for its simplex and globally shared constraints, and mode \(\mathrm R\) does the analogous thing for \(b_j\).  Hence no unsupported propagation of an inactive endpoint into the observed column span is made.  Mode \(\mathrm E\) retains the whole split vector \(s_e\), which is essential because its coordinates enter the IV residual equations.

Take the product of the local mode lists over the four response-cycle cells.  Use a single normalized variable \(b_i\) for the two occurrences of response type \(i\).  Therefore equality of shared endpoints is imposed, rather than inferred.  Refine each coordinate of each \(b_i\) into zero or positive support, each split or rank-two coefficient into its displayed zero/interior alternatives, and each finite endpoint equality, inequality, line incidence, and pivot into its sign alternatives.  Every refinement is a finite conjunction of polynomial equalities and strict inequalities over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  Equations (2) and the rank-one normal-form lemma prove that every point of \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) enters at least one refinement.  Direct substitution in each local cell equation proves the reverse inclusion.  Thus the union of these charts is exactly \(\mathcal C_A(T)\), including simultaneous rank-one cells, coincident endpoints, inactive response rows, and forced coefficient zeros.

For design B, fix one of these cycle charts and a positive projective vector \(\rho\).  At each response type, \(\mathrm{thm:iv\text{-}residual\text{-}forest}\) gives an exhaustive alternative: both incident residual vectors vanish, exactly one vanishes and the branch is empty, or both are nonzero and negatively proportional.  In the last case choose the first nonzero coordinate as pivot and refine its sign; this is a finite disjoint pivot list.  Active links determine positive cell-margin ratios.  Since the active graph is a subgraph of the four-cycle, it is either a forest or the whole cycle.  Forest ratios propagate from one positive scale per component, and in the whole-cycle case consistency is equivalent to the single product-one equation.  Positivity of the scales and their normalization give all and only the positive margins.  Finally, enumerate a pair \(z<z'\) and a sign for
\[
q^X_zg(z')-q^X_{z'}g(z)\ne0.
\]
The residual-forest theorem proves that these refinements are necessary and sufficient for \(\mathcal C_B(T)\).  This establishes the claimed structural union before any target test.

Each resulting chart is a one-copy semialgebraic set: its variables are one collection of endpoints, coefficients, and, in design B, projective and margin coordinates.  Clear only denominators whose positivity or nonzero pivot condition is already recorded.  The exact component and roadmap algorithms in \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}components}\) first return a description and a sample point \(x_C\) for every semialgebraically connected component \(C\).  Only after this step form
\[
G_C=\{(x,t):x\in C,\ t=\tau_C(x)\}
\]
and compute its target projection by one-block elimination.  Put \(t_0=\tau_C(x_C)\).  To avoid confusing a positive-dimensional projection with the number of decomposition cells, refine the same component by
\[
\bigl(\tau_{C,1}(x)-t_{0,1}\bigr)^2+
\bigl(\tau_{C,2}(x)-t_{0,2}\bigr)^2>0. \tag{3}
\]
The cited realizability algorithm decides (3).  If it is nonempty, its sampled point \(x_C'\) has a different target.  If it is empty, \(\tau_C\equiv t_0\) on all of \(C\).  This is a one-copy component calculation, not a pair-of-fibers predicate.  Comparing the Thom encodings of the finitely many component constants then decides global agreement across components and overlapping support charts.

The sample value \(t_0\) is represented by a real-univariate encoding over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\); adjoining that encoded algebraic element makes every coefficient in (3) effective for the same sign and realizability routines.  Moreover, chart existence, component existence, and target-projection tests eliminate only latent chart coordinates, so their final signs and Thom comparisons depend only on the observed input \(\zeta\).  They are therefore observable tests.

When all constants agree, a sampled target coordinate is already an exact output.  If field arithmetic has constructed it as a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), the compiler returns that expression.  Otherwise the sampling and elimination algorithms return a real-univariate representation with Thom data, and the compiler retains that encoding even if an unperformed simplification could place the number back in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  If agreement fails, either (3) supplies two points in one component or two constant components supply one sampled point each.  The previously proved structural union makes both legal cycle points.  The cycle-to-SCM lift then gives two full SCMs with the same observables and, in design A, the same supplied margins.  This proves every asserted output and completes the open-ended question.
body.justification: This theorem closes the sole structural gap by proving the L/R/E/D and rank-two chart union before any component calculation.
body.gap: Earlier rounds covered all-rank-two cells and conditional IV margin elimination but not simultaneous equal endpoints, inactive rows, and support faces.
body.consumer: The global atlas, complexity theorem, and inference procedures now have an exhaustive finite chart family.
